missions.title: Counting Market
missions.subtitle: Count the village supplies
missions.guide: Tap the correct word block. Help the market count its supplies!
missions.reminder: There is goes with one thing. There are goes with more than one.

tasks.prompt: One apple is on the stall. There ___ one apple.
tasks.hint: One apple is one thing. Choose is.
tasks.explain: There is one apple. Use is for one thing.

tasks.prompt: Three bags are on the stall. There ___ three bags.
tasks.hint: Three bags are more than one. Choose are.
tasks.explain: There are three bags. Use are for more than one thing.

tasks.prompt: We have two boxes. There are two ___ here.
tasks.hint: More than one box: boxes.
tasks.explain: Use boxes when there is more than one box.

tasks.prompt: Two children visit the market. There are two ___.
tasks.hint: One child. Two children.
tasks.explain: Children is the word for more than one child.

tasks.prompt: Two mice hide by the stall. There are two ___.
tasks.hint: One mouse. Two mice.
tasks.explain: Mice is the word for more than one mouse.

missions.title: Friendship Bridge
missions.subtitle: Help your friends cross
missions.guide: Tap the correct pronoun block. Build a bridge for your friends!
missions.reminder: Use he for a boy, she for a girl, and they for two or more people.

tasks.prompt: Amir is a boy. ___ is my friend.
tasks.full: Amir is a boy. He is my friend.
tasks.hint: Amir is a boy. Choose He.
tasks.explain: He takes the place of Amir.

tasks.prompt: Mei is a girl. ___ is reading.
tasks.full: Mei is a girl. She is reading.
tasks.hint: Mei is a girl. Choose She.
tasks.explain: She takes the place of Mei.

tasks.prompt: Amir and Mei play together. ___ are friends.
tasks.full: Amir and Mei play together. They are friends.
tasks.hint: Amir and Mei are two people. Choose They.
tasks.explain: They takes the place of Amir and Mei.

tasks.prompt: This cap belongs to Amir. It is ___ cap.
tasks.hint: The cap belongs to a boy. Choose his.
tasks.explain: His cap means the cap belongs to Amir.

tasks.prompt: This ruler belongs to Mei. It is ___ ruler.
tasks.hint: The ruler belongs to a girl. Choose her.
tasks.explain: Her ruler means the ruler belongs to Mei.

missions.title: Routine Train
missions.subtitle: Build a daily routine
missions.guide: Tap the word carriages in order. Build a routine to move the train!
missions.reminder: Use play with I or they. Use plays with he or she.

tasks.prompt: Tell us your morning routine. Start with I.
tasks.hint: Start with I eat. Finish with every day.
tasks.explain: Every day tells us this is a routine. Use eat after I.

tasks.prompt: Tell us how Mei goes to school. Start with She.
tasks.hint: Start with She. Then put walks.
tasks.explain: She walks to school. Use walks after she for a routine.

tasks.prompt: Tell us about the friends. Start with They.
tasks.hint: Start with They play. Finish with every day.
tasks.explain: They play football every day. Use play after they.

tasks.prompt: Amir always packs his bag. Start with He.
tasks.hint: Start with He always. Put packs next.
tasks.explain: Always means every time. Use packs after he.

tasks.prompt: Tell us what your group does after school. Start with We.
tasks.hint: Start with We read. Finish with after school.
tasks.explain: We read books after school. Use read after we.

missions.title: Action River
missions.subtitle: Build actions happening now
missions.guide: Put the word blocks in order. Build a boat with an action happening now!
missions.reminder: For an action happening now, use am, is or are with an -ing word.

tasks.prompt: You are reading now. Start with I.
tasks.hint: Start with I am. Add reading a book.
tasks.explain: I am reading a book. Use am with I.

tasks.prompt: Mei is singing now. Start with She.
tasks.hint: Start with She is. Put singing next.
tasks.explain: She is singing now. Use is with she.

tasks.prompt: The boys are playing now. Start with They.
tasks.hint: Start with They are. Put playing next.
tasks.explain: They are playing football. Use are with they.

tasks.prompt: Amir is eating now. Start with He.
tasks.hint: Start with He is. Add eating an apple.
tasks.explain: He is eating an apple. Use is with he.

tasks.prompt: Your group is drawing now. Start with We.
tasks.hint: Start with We are. Put drawing next.
tasks.explain: We are drawing now. Use are with we.

missions.title: Yesterday Mine
missions.subtitle: Find words from the past
missions.guide: Tap the correct word block. Find a gem for each action from yesterday!
missions.reminder: Yesterday is in the past. Play becomes played. Go becomes went.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ a game.
tasks.hint: Yesterday is in the past. Play becomes played.
tasks.explain: Played tells us the action happened in the past.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, Mei ___ her grandma.
tasks.hint: Visit becomes visited for the past.
tasks.explain: Visited tells us Mei saw her grandma in the past.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, Amir ___ to the park.
tasks.full: Yesterday, Amir went to the park.
tasks.hint: Go changes to went in the past.
tasks.explain: Went is the past word for go.

tasks.prompt: Last night, we ___ rice.
tasks.hint: Eat changes to ate in the past.
tasks.explain: Ate tells us the meal happened last night.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, they ___ a film.
tasks.hint: Watch becomes watched for the past.
tasks.explain: Watched tells us the action happened yesterday.

missions.title: Linking Portal
missions.subtitle: Join the story blocks
missions.guide: Read the story clue. Tap a linking word to open the portal!
missions.reminder: And adds. Or gives a choice. But joins different or opposite ideas.

tasks.prompt: We need both things. Bring a pencil ___ a ruler.
tasks.full: Bring a pencil and a ruler.
tasks.hint: We need both a pencil and a ruler. Use and.
tasks.explain: And joins the two things we need.

tasks.prompt: Choose one drink. Would you like milk ___ water?
tasks.full: Would you like milk or water?
tasks.hint: You choose one drink. Use or.
tasks.explain: Or gives you a choice between two drinks.

tasks.prompt: Join these opposite ideas: I like cats, ___ I do not like snakes.
tasks.full: I like cats, but I do not like snakes.
tasks.hint: One animal is liked. The other is not. Use but to show the difference.
tasks.explain: But connects the different ideas about cats and snakes.

tasks.prompt: Both friends are here. Amir ___ Mei are in the village.
tasks.full: Amir and Mei are in the village.
tasks.hint: Both friends are here. Use and to name both.
tasks.explain: And connects the names of the two friends.

tasks.prompt: Join these surprising ideas: The box is small, ___ it is heavy.
tasks.full: The box is small, but it is heavy.
tasks.hint: The box is small, yet it is heavy. Use but to show the surprise.
tasks.explain: But shows the difference: the box is small, yet it is heavy.

missions.title: Animal Rescue
missions.subtitle: Give the cat a safe place
missions.guide: Tap the cat, then tap its place. You can also drag the cat!
missions.reminder: Read the place word. In is inside. Behind is at the back. Between is in the middle.

tasks.prompt: The cat is in the box.
tasks.full: The cat is in the box.
tasks.hint: In means inside. Tap the inside of the box.
tasks.explain: In the box means inside the box.

tasks.prompt: The cat is on the table.
tasks.full: The cat is on the table.
tasks.hint: On means on top. Tap the table top.
tasks.explain: On the table means on top of the table.

tasks.prompt: The cat is under the table.
tasks.full: The cat is under the table.
tasks.hint: Under means below. Tap the space below the table.
tasks.explain: Under the table means below the table.

tasks.prompt: The cat is behind the tree.
tasks.full: The cat is behind the tree.
tasks.hint: Behind means at the back. Tap the space behind the tree.
tasks.explain: Behind the tree means at the back of the tree.

tasks.prompt: The cat is between the rocks.
tasks.full: The cat is between the rocks.
tasks.hint: Between means in the middle of two things. Tap the space between the rocks.
tasks.explain: Between the rocks means in the middle of the two rocks.

missions.title: Size Castle
missions.subtitle: Compare two objects
missions.guide: Look at both objects. Tap the one that matches the words!
missions.reminder: Taller and shorter compare heights. Bigger and smaller compare sizes.

tasks.prompt: Choose the taller tower.
tasks.full: Tower B is taller than Tower A.
tasks.hint: Look for the tower that is higher than the other.
tasks.explain: Tower B is taller than Tower A.

tasks.prompt: Choose the shorter tower.
tasks.full: Tower A is shorter than Tower B.
tasks.hint: Look for the tower that is lower than the other.
tasks.explain: Tower A is shorter than Tower B.

tasks.prompt: Choose the bigger chest.
tasks.full: Chest A is bigger than Chest B.
tasks.hint: Look for the chest that takes up more space.
tasks.explain: Chest A is bigger than Chest B.

tasks.prompt: Choose the smaller chest.
tasks.full: Chest B is smaller than Chest A.
tasks.hint: Look for the chest that takes up less space.
tasks.explain: Chest B is smaller than Chest A.

tasks.prompt: Choose the taller tower for the flag.
tasks.full: Tower A is taller than Tower B.
tasks.hint: Compare the two towers. Which one is higher?
tasks.explain: Tower A is taller than Tower B. Taller compares two heights.

rules: There is one ... · There are two ...
Use is for one. Use are for more than one. Some plural words change.
One child, two children. One mouse, two mice.
Use he for a boy, she for a girl, and they for two or more people. His and her show who owns something.
Mei is a girl. She has a ruler. It is her ruler.
I play · She plays · They play
Use these words for routines. Always means every time.
Use am with I, is with he or she, and are with we or they.
play → played · go → went · eat → ate
Yesterday and last night tell us an action is in the past.
Yesterday, Amir went to the park.
and = add · or = choose · but = show a difference
Choose a word that matches the ideas you want to join.
I like cats, but I do not like snakes.
Inside · on top · below · at the back · in the middle of two things.
The cat is between the rocks.
tall → taller · big → bigger · small → smaller
Use taller or shorter for height. Use bigger or smaller for size.
Tower A is taller than Tower B.

curriculum.note: Original supported practice for pupils needing short, scaffolded tasks. Content selects Year 3 grammar and recycled Year 1–2 language: plurals, pronouns, present simple and continuous, simple past, conjunctions, position words and short-adjective comparisons. Hints, audio, small choices and retry feedback support learning. Game points do not determine a DSKP performance level.
